place: Chaweng Noi, Ko Samui District, Surat Thani, Thailand
title: Balinese-Inspired 5-Bedroom Hillside Villa with Infinity Pool, Chaweng Noi
note: Chef & massage on request · utilities metered
blurb: A five-bedroom villa high on the hillside above Chaweng Noi, where a long infinity pool runs out over the palm canopy toward open water. Timber-lined ceilings, granite boulders left in place and walls that slide fully away give the house a Balinese ease, while the interiors carry colour and collected art. Two levels, a lawn on the seaward side and covered parking for three.
detail:
Set high on the hillside above Chaweng Noi, on Koh Samui's east coast, this five-bedroom villa is built to sit inside its view rather than merely face it. The approach climbs steeply — a 4WD is worth having for the last stretch — and delivers you to a house arranged over two levels with covered parking for three cars and a lawn falling away toward the water. The beaches, restaurants and nightlife of Chaweng are a few minutes down the hill.

The design takes its cue from Bali without pastiche: pitched ceilings lined in warm timber, deep overhangs, and glass walls that slide entirely away so the main pavilion becomes an open-sided room between the pool and the horizon. The natural granite boulders on the site have been kept and built around — one forms the backdrop to a built-in outdoor sofa in turquoise, another anchors the pool terrace.

The pool runs the length of the terrace with an infinity edge disappearing into the sea view, framed by palms and the green hillside below. Behind it the living room opens on two sides, furnished with deep sofas, a live-edge timber dining table and a collection of colourful art and textiles that gives the house real character. The open-plan American-style kitchen sits alongside in white with an island and breakfast stools, and a second dining terrace catches the morning light.

Five bedrooms are spread across both levels — four with king beds and one twin — several opening directly to the lawn or a sea-facing terrace, all air-conditioned with ceiling fans and hung with framed art. The four bathrooms are finished in pale grey stone with walk-in rain showers, twin vessel basins on timber counters, and one carrying a freestanding tub set at a window over the bay.

Bed linen and towels are changed every three days, high-speed fibre WiFi covers the house, and there is a laptop-friendly workspace. The management team can arrange a private chef, in-villa massage, car and motorbike hire, speedboat charters and island tours, along with cots and high chairs for families. Electricity and water are metered and settled at checkout.
